record.hypothesis: Across all four datasets, replace only the existing projected frequency input with z_i=2*tanh(((log1p(f_i)-mu)/sigma)/2), using category-specific training-item counts and training-only mu,sigma; assign zero to padding and unseen items. Bounding extreme frequency features may reduce popularity-driven attention distortion while retaining frequency ordering. Keep inverse-frequency embedding scaling, learned embeddings, projection, HSTU topology, readout, loss and optimizer fixed. Persist the transformed feature buffer and restore it identically through the predictor writer, retaining one model/checkpoint per category.

category_rationales.rationale: Across all four category models, bound the existing standardized training-frequency input with 2*tanh(z/2) to reduce extreme feature magnitudes while preserving frequency ordering. Padding and unseen items retain zero. The existing checkpoint buffer and generated predictor restore the transformed feature directly. Learned embeddings, inverse-frequency scaling, projection, HSTU topology, readout, loss and optimizer remain fixed.
